{{Current events|year=2021|month=01|day=18|content=
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Central African Republic Civil War]]
**Two [[United Nations peacekeeping|United Nation peacekeepers]], from [[Gabon]] and [[Morocco]], are killed in an ambush by [[anti-balaka]] insurgents near [[Bangassou]], [[Central African Republic]], according to [[MINUSCA]]. [https://reliefweb.int/report/central-african-republic/two-un-peacekeepers-killed-ambush-central-african-republic (Relief Web)]
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2014–present)|Yemeni Civil War]]
**[[Houthi movement|Houthi]] forces and pro-[[Government of Yemen|government]] [[Republic of Yemen Armed Forces|troops]] clash in the [[port city]] of [[Al Hudaydah]], leaving at least 23 people dead. The fighting centered around the government-controlled [[Ad Durayhimi District]] in the south of the city. Houthi-run [[Almasirah]] network claims "dozens" of government fighters have been killed. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2021-01/19/c_139678345.htm (Xinhuanet)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
**[[Prime Minister of Malaysia|Prime Minister]] [[Muhyiddin Yassin]] announces a new [[Malaysian ringgit|RM]]15 billion economic assistance package, the [[Malaysia]]n Economic and Rakyat Protection Assistance Package, which is expected to reduce the impact of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] on the [[Economy of Malaysia|Malaysian economy]]. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/malaysia-pm-muhyiddin-economic-aid-package-covid-19-13986120 (CNA)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong]]
****[[Hong Kong]] reports 107 new confirmed cases, which is the first time in nearly a month that more than 100 cases are reported and brings the total number of confirmed cases in the city to 9,664. This sudden rise in cases is partially due to an outbreak among ethnic minorities. [https://amp.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/health-environment/article/3118122/hong-kong-fourth-wave-mandatory-covid-19-testing (''South China Morning Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] reports a record 9,475 recoveries, including 2,802 from [[Jakarta]], bringing the nationwide total of recoveries to 745,935. [https://news.detik.com/berita/d-5338810/kasus-sembuh-corona-pecah-rekor-hari-ini-terbanyak-di-dki-jakarta (detikNews)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Japan]] detects possible community spread of the [[Variant of Concern 202012/01|B.1.1.7 variant]] in three people from [[Shizuoka Prefecture|Shizuoka]] with no known travel history. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2021/01/18/national/japan-uk-coronavirus-variant/ (''The Japan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Nepal]]
****[[Nepal]] reports their first case of a [[Variant of Concern 202012/01|new variant]] of [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]] in three people who travelled to the [[United Kingdom]] three weeks ago and later tested positive. [https://kathmandupost.com/health/2021/01/18/new-variant-of-coronavirus-confirmed-in-three-persons-who-had-returned-from-the-uk (''The Kathmandu Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkmenistan]]
****[[Turkmenistan]] registers the [[Gam-COVID-Vac|Sputnik V]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] despite having no confirmed cases in the country, according to the Russian Direct Investment Fund. It becomes the first country in [[Central Asia]] to approve a Russian-made vaccine. [https://www.rferl.org/a/turkmenistan-covis-19-sputnik-vaccination-russian-authorities/31051162.html (RFE/RL)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Czech Republic]]
****The [[Czech Republic]] confirms the detection of the [[Variant of Concern 202012/01|B.1.1.7 variant]] that originated in the [[United Kingdom]]. [https://www.ceskenoviny.cz/zpravy/v-cesku-se-potvrdil-vyskyt-takzvane-britske-mutace-koronaviru/1983240 (CTK)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****[[Bavaria]] detects a new [[variants of SARS-CoV-2|variant]] of [[SARS-CoV-2]] in 35 newly-infected patients in [[Garmisch-Partenkirchen]], which is different from [[Variant_of_Concern_202012/01|the strain]] originating from the [[United Kingdom]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/germany-new-covid-variant-found-in-bavaria/a-56269615 (DW)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]]
****Hair salons, health centers, car inspection stations, and non-essential shops in [[Greece]] reopen for the first time since November after the [[Government of Greece|government]] eased a nationwide [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] in order to revitalize the retail sectors. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/greek-work-places-gradually-re-opening/2114270# (Anadolu Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]
****[[Portugal]] reports a record 167 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 9,028. [http://sicnoticias.pt/especiais/coronavirus/2021-01-18-Portugal-com-mais-167-mortes-e-6.702-casos-de-covid-19-nas-ultimas-24-horas-1 (SIC Noticias)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****The [[Ministry of Health (Spain)|Spanish Health Ministry]] reports a record 84,287 new cases in the [[Spain|country]] over the weekend, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2,336,451. [https://www.eldiario.es/sociedad/espana-registra-nuevos-casos-coronavirus-muertes-durante-semana_1_6862144.html (elDiario.es)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****Outgoing [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] signs an executive order that allows travel restrictions on [[Brazil]], the [[United Kingdom]], and [[Europe]] to be lifted after January 26. However, incoming [[White House Press Secretary|Press Secretary]] [[Jen Psaki]] says that the restrictions are expected to remain in place. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-usa-travel-exclusi/exclusive-trump-lifting-covid-19-travel-restrictions-on-europe-uk-brazil-sources-idUSKBN29N20Y (Reuters)] [https://edition.cnn.com/2021/01/18/politics/trump-covid-travel-restrictions/index.html (CNN)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
****[[California]] becomes the first [[U.S. state]] to surpass three million cases of [[COVID-19]]. [https://apnews.com/article/los-angeles-coronavirus-pandemic-california-coronavirus-vaccine-us-news-51a97c9d7fd02e5fb66553a27603ba4e (AP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Maryland]], [[COVID-19 vaccine]]
****[[Governor of Maryland|Maryland Governor]] [[Larry Hogan]] receives the [[Moderna]] [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] at the [[Maryland State House|State House]] in [[Annapolis, Maryland|Annapolis]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/coronavirus/hogan-vaccine-maryland-virginia-district/2021/01/18/3221a38c-599a-11eb-a976-bad6431e03e2_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Morocco]]
***[[Morocco]] reports its first case of the [[Variant of Concern 202012/01|B.1.1.7 variant]] in the [[Tanger-Med|Port of Tangier Med]]. [https://www.moroccoworldnews.com/2021/01/332373/morocco-records-1st-case-of-new-covid-19-strain/ (Morocco World News)]
**[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the environment]]
***The [[International Energy Agency]] reports that global [[methane emissions]] in 2020 amounted to about 70 million metric tons, which is 10 percent lower than the estimated amount of methane emissions in 2019. The agency cites the decline in industrial activities, as a result of the pandemic, and the introduction of new emission regulations for the reduction in emissions. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-01-18/global-methane-emissions-equaled-europe-s-carbon-footprint-in-2020 (Bloomberg)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Germany–Russia relations]]
**[[Germany]] condemns the arrest of [[opposition to Vladimir Putin in Russia|opposition]] politician and activist [[Alexei Navalny]] upon his return to [[Russia]] yesterday. [[German Foreign Minister]] [[Heiko Maas]] calls the arrest "utterly incomprehensible" and calls for Navalny's immediate release. Likewise, British, Danish, and other European [[diplomat]]s also condemn the arrest. [https://www.dw.com/en/alexei-navalnys-detainment-is-utterly-incomprehensible-says-germanys-maas/a-56257961 (DW)]
*[[South Korea–United States relations]]
**[[South Korean President]] [[Moon Jae-in]] urges incoming [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] to learn from the policies, both positive and negative, of [[Donald Trump]] towards [[North Korea]] and says that the North has a "clear willingness to denuclearize if [[Washington, D.C.|Washington]] and [[Pyongyang]] could find mutually agreeable steps to decrease the nuclear threat and ensure the North's security". [https://apnews.com/article/donald-trump-north-korea-seoul-nuclear-weapons-south-korea-1dc2f8c8df7c7916baccb167cf3cc687 (AP)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
**[[Fashion Institute of Technology]] student Nicholas Moncada is arrested for allegedly posting "Outside [[Nancy Pelosi|Pelosi]]'s office" on [[Instagram]] and livestreaming the [[2021 storming of the United States Capitol|storming]] of the [[United States Capitol]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/US/capitol-rioter-allegedly-posted-pelosis-office-instagram-arrested/story?id=75324078 (ABC News)]
*[[Corruption in South Korea]]
**The [[Chief operating officer|COO]] of [[Samsung]], [[Lee Jae-yong (businessman)|Lee Jae-yong]], is sentenced to two and a half years in prison on charges of bribery. Lee was convicted of bribing former South Korean President [[Park Geun-hye]] and was arrested in the courtroom following the verdict. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/01/18/business/south-korea-samsung-prison-lee.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[Central American migrant caravans]]
**[[Law enforcement in Guatemala|Guatemalan police]] report that around 4,000 United States-bound [[Honduran diaspora|Honduran migrants]] held up at the [[Guatemala–Honduras border]] since January 16 have been dispersed. Police have used various [[riot control]] methods to disperse migrants. [https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1385507/guatemalan-security-forces-break-up-us-bound-migrant-caravan (AFP via ''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]
*The [[Ministry of the Interior (Tunisia)|Tunisian interior ministry]] deploys the [[Tunisian National Guard|national guard]] in several cities across [[Tunisia|the country]] and reports that a total of 632 people have been arrested following a series of riots that first occurred January 15, a day after the [[Government of Tunisia|government]] imposed a nationwide [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] in response to an increase in [[COVID-19 pandemic in Tunisia|COVID-19 cases]]. [https://www.dailysabah.com/world/asia-pacific/tunisia-detains-600-deploys-troops-as-protests-over-moribund-economy-spread-across-country (AFP via ''Daily Sabah'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2020–21 Central African general election]]
**The constitutional court of the [[Central African Republic]] confirms the re-election of [[President of the Central African Republic|President]] [[Faustin-Archange Touadéra]], despite a voter turnout of only 35.25 percent. The low turnout was attributed to the hindrance of [[polling station]]s from operating and voters unable to cast their ballots as [[Central African Republic Civil War|various armed groups currently control]] roughly two-thirds of the country, thus prompting most opposition candidates and activists to call the election farce and fraudulent. [https://www.africanews.com/2021/01/18/central-african-republic-top-court-confirms-touadera-election-win// (AFP via Africanews)]
